text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Palestinian dawn glows in Hebron as Israeli occupation disappears.
- Six labour unions oppose new organisation of unified labour union. Dissenting unions to meet today.
- Parliament's Palestine committee meets international refugee experts for discussions on Palestinian refugees in Jordan.
- Sudanese ambassador praises Jordan's support for his country in the face of external aggression.

- Transport Minister Lawzi says 100 trucks to be bought for Iraq-Jordan Land Transport company ahead of expected increase in trade between the two countries. Purchases will increase company fleet to 450 trucks, still half its 1985 level.
- Head of Jordan's Gulf War reparation committee says payment to U.N. reparation fund means compensation payments to Jordanians can begin.

- Finance Minister Awad says new list of customs duties to be issued shortly. Duties on cars will be replaced with other fees which will mean no change for consumers from new system. Maximum customs duty expected to be 30 to 40 percent.
- Jordan and Iraq expected to sign agreements on 1997 trade and oil accords today, Iraqi press says.
